gateway.description:
Gateway API configuration, consumed by `common.gateway.*`. The successor to `ingress`, and
an independent switch from it: a cluster migrating between an Ingress controller and a Gateway
implementation runs both for a while.

The division of labour is the API's, not this chart's. A `Gateway` — the listeners, the
address, the certificates — belongs to the cluster operator; an application owns only the
`HTTPRoute` that attaches to it. So the default here is route-only, and `create` is for
installs that have no cluster-wide Gateway to attach to.

addresses.description: Addresses requested for the created Gateway, e.g. a fixed `IPAddress`.
addresses.title: addresses

allowedRoutes.description:
Which routes may attach to the created Gateway's listeners. Defaults to `Same`: a Gateway
this chart owns should not be attachable from another namespace unless that is asked for.
allowedRoutes.title: allowedRoutes

annotations.description: Annotations for the HTTPRoute and the created Gateway. Values may contain Go templates.
annotations.title: annotations

backendRefs.description:
Backends for rules that name none. Defaults to this chart's own Service. Weights are
honoured, so a traffic split needs no custom rule.
backendRefs.title: backendRefs

create.description:
Also create the Gateway itself. Leave off when the cluster already runs one — that is the
normal case, and one Gateway per application usually means one load balancer per
application. When on, a route that names no parent attaches to it automatically.
create.title: create

enabled.title: enabled

filters.description:
Filters applied to the default rule: `RequestHeaderModifier`, `ResponseHeaderModifier`,
`RequestRedirect`, `URLRewrite`, `RequestMirror`, `ExtensionRef`. This is where an
Ingress controller's annotations end up, as typed fields. Ignored when `rules` is set.
filters.title: filters

gatewayClassName.description:
GatewayClass that programs the created Gateway, e.g. `cilium`, `istio`, `envoy-gateway`,
`nginx`. Required by `create`; a Gateway without one is never reconciled. Ignored otherwise.
gatewayClassName.title: gatewayClassName

hostnames.description:
Hostnames the route serves. Values may contain Go templates.

Required unless `create` is set. A route with no hostnames matches every name its listener
accepts: on a Gateway this chart owns that is harmless, and sometimes the point — an install
reached by address has no DNS name to state. On a shared Gateway it means taking over traffic
meant for other applications, so the render refuses it.
hostnames.title: hostnames

A second route that redirects plaintext traffic to HTTPS. Under Ingress this was a
controller-specific annotation; Gateway API expresses it as a typed `RequestRedirect`

sectionName.description:
Listener to bind the redirect to. Must be the plaintext one: attached to every listener,

listeners.description:
Listeners for the created Gateway, replacing the derived ones entirely. Reach for this
when a listener needs its own hostname or certificate.

parentRefs.description:
Gateways the route attaches to. Each entry takes `name` and optionally `namespace`,
`sectionName` (a single listener), `port`, `group` and `kind`; the API's defaults are filled
in. Values may contain Go templates.

A route that names no parent is accepted by the API server and then does nothing — no
listener ever programs it — so this is required unless `create` is set.
Example:
```yaml
parentRefs:
  - name: shared-gateway
    namespace: gateway-system
    sectionName: https
```
parentRefs.title: parentRefs

path.description: Path prefix for the default rule. Ignored when `rules` is set.
path.title: path

rules.description:
Routing rules, in full `HTTPRouteRule` form (`matches`, `filters`, `backendRefs`,
`timeouts`). An entry that omits `backendRefs` inherits this chart's Service, so a rule that
only narrows the path does not have to restate where the traffic goes.

Left empty, the route gets one rule matching `path` as a prefix — the Gateway API equivalent
of a single-path Ingress, and a complete configuration together with `hostnames`.

timeouts.description:
Timeouts for the default rule: `request` and `backendRequest`, as Go durations. Ignored
when `rules` is set.
timeouts.title: timeouts

tls.description:
TLS for the created Gateway's HTTPS listener. Ignored without `create`, and irrelevant
when attaching to somebody else's Gateway — the certificate is theirs.

certificateRefs.description:

convention by which one is looked up from the hostname. A ref naming another namespace
additionally needs a `ReferenceGrant` there, which this chart deliberately does not create
— a grant is the target namespace owner's to give.
certificateRefs.title: certificateRefs

networkPolicy.description:
Network policy configuration.

Every generated egress rule is scoped by a `to:` selector. An egress rule that lists only
ports is not a restriction — the NetworkPolicy API reads a missing `to` as "any
destination", so such a policy permits traffic to every in-cluster service and to the
cloud metadata endpoint.

cilium.description:
Cilium-only additions, used when `engine` is `cilium` or `both`. Everything above is
translated into the CiliumNetworkPolicy automatically; these are the rules the portable API
has no way to express.

Note that `extraIngress`, `extraEgress` and the per-section `customRules` above are *not*
carried over: those are verbatim `networking.k8s.io/v1` rule objects and are not valid CNP.
The fields below are their counterparts.

description.description:
`spec.description`, which Cilium surfaces in `cilium policy get` and in Hubble flow
verdicts. The one place to record *why* a rule exists where an operator debugging a drop
will actually see it.
description.title: description

customRules.description: Additional egress rules in CiliumNetworkPolicy form, appended verbatim.
customRules.title: customRules

dnsMatchPatterns.description:
What the DNS proxy may resolve, e.g. `- matchPattern: "*.example.com"`. Defaults to
everything, which only permits the lookup — an answer is still only reachable if some
rule allows the address.
dnsMatchPatterns.title: dnsMatchPatterns

entityPorts.description: Restrict the `toEntities` rule to specific ports. Empty means all ports.
entityPorts.title: entityPorts

fqdnPorts.description: Ports the `toFQDNs` rule allows. Defaults to TCP/443.
fqdnPorts.title: fqdnPorts

httpRules.description:
L7 HTTP rules layered onto the `toFQDNs` rule, e.g.
`- method: GET` / `path: "/v1/.*"`. Turns "may reach this host" into "may make these
requests to this host". Costs a proxy hop per connection.
httpRules.title: httpRules

toEntities.description:
Named destination sets, e.g. `world` for everything outside the cluster, or
`kube-apiserver`. Not a synonym for the `egress.cidr`/`except` translation: `world` does
not carve out the cloud metadata endpoint the way those defaults do.
toEntities.title: toEntities

toFQDNs.description:
Destinations by name rather than by address, e.g. `- matchName: api.example.com` or
`- matchPattern: "*.example.com"`. This is the rule the CIDR-based `egress.https` was
always a poor approximation of: "may reach the internet on 443" permits every public host
that exists, where this permits the ones the application actually talks to.

Enforced against the addresses Cilium's DNS proxy saw returned for the name, so
`egress.dns.enabled` must stay on — the render fails if it is not.
toFQDNs.title: toFQDNs

enableDefaultDeny.description:
State default-deny explicitly rather than relying on it being implied by the presence of
rules. This is what makes the intentional default-deny case — a policy with an empty rule
list — actually deny, instead of being treated as no policy at all. Requires Cilium 1.16+.
enableDefaultDeny.title: enableDefaultDeny

extraEgress.description: Extra egress rules in CiliumNetworkPolicy form, appended regardless of `egress.enabled`.
extraEgress.title: extraEgress

extraIngress.description:
Extra ingress rules in CiliumNetworkPolicy form, appended regardless of

extraIngress.title: extraIngress

customRules.description: Additional ingress rules in CiliumNetworkPolicy form, appended verbatim.

fromEntities.title: fromEntities

engine.description:
Which policy dialect to render. `kubernetes` emits the portable
`networking.k8s.io/v1` pair; `cilium` emits `CiliumNetworkPolicy`, which can express FQDN
destinations, named entities and L7 rules that the portable API cannot; `both` emits both,
for the window in which a cluster is migrating between CNIs.

The engine picks the dialect, not the rules — every value below is translated either way, so
switching is a one-line change. `both` is additive rather than stricter: policies selecting
one pod union their allowances, so it is a migration setting and not a hardening one.
engine.title: engine

also set, so it costs nothing on a chart exposed through an Ingress.

definition the one `gateway.parentRefs` names, so both fields below are derived from it.
Restating the Gateway's identity here would be a second place to edit on a rename, and a
policy that names the wrong Gateway looks correct and blocks all inbound traffic.

`fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`); `none` applies nothing. Identity fields
(`runAsUser`, `runAsGroup`, `fsGroup`) are always left to the chart, since they must match

prometheusRule.description:
Prometheus recording and alerting rules, consumed by `common.prometheus.rules.*`. Unlike the
dashboards there is only one carrier — `PrometheusRule` is already the operator's own CRD — and
no per-object cross-namespace grant: which namespaces a Prometheus loads rules from is decided
by `ruleNamespaceSelector` and `ruleSelector` on the Prometheus custom resource.

enabled.description:
Create a PrometheusRule from the chart's rule files. Requires the `monitoring.coreos.com/v1`
CRDs; `common.prometheus.rules.errors` fails the render loudly rather than silently dropping
the object when they are absent.
enabled.title: enabled

labels.description:
Extra labels, templated. This is the only half of rule discovery a chart controls: a
cluster whose Prometheus selects `release: kube-prometheus-stack` needs that label here, or
the rules are created and never loaded.
labels.title: labels

scope.description:
Confine the rules to a subset of the cluster's series. A `PrometheusRule` is not scoped to
the namespace it lives in, so `up{job="api"} == 0` matches somebody else's `api` job in
another namespace and two installs of one chart alert on each other. Rather than parse PromQL
in a Go template, the rule files mark every selector with an always-true placeholder matcher
and the library swaps it for a real one — see the note in `_prometheus.tpl`. Consuming charts
normally derive `matcher` rather than exposing it raw.

matcher.description:
What to swap it for, e.g. `namespace="prod"`. Empty disables the substitution; the
placeholder is left in place, which is correct, because it is already a no-op matcher.
matcher.title: matcher

placeholder.description:
The literal placeholder written into the rule files, e.g. `myapp_scope=~".*"`. Empty
disables the substitution and the files install exactly as vendored.
placeholder.title: placeholder

workload — the right answer for a single-user instance. PostgreSQL is upstream's
recommendation for anything larger and is the only engine this chart can bundle.

Publishing through the Gateway API. The cluster operator owns the `Gateway`; this chart
owns the `HTTPRoute` that attaches to it.

annotations.description: Annotations for the HTTPRoute and, when created, the Gateway.
annotations.title: annotations

create.description: Also create a Gateway, for an install with no cluster-wide one to attach to.

Create an HTTPRoute. Requires the Gateway API CRDs; the chart refuses to render without
them rather than dropping the route silently.

filters.description:
HTTPRoute filters — header manipulation, request mirroring, URL rewriting. These are the
typed replacement for what Ingress expressed as controller-specific annotations.
filters.title: filters

gatewayClassName.description:
GatewayClass for the created Gateway. Required when `gateway.create` is set — a Gateway
without one is never reconciled by anything.
gatewayClassName.title: gatewayClassName

hostnames.description:
Hostnames the route serves. Used as the default for `paperless.url`. Required unless
`gateway.create` is set, because a route with no hostnames matches every hostname its
listener accepts — on a shared Gateway that quietly steals other applications' traffic.
hostnames.title: hostnames

httpsRedirect.description: A second route that redirects plaintext requests to HTTPS.

enabled.description: Create the redirect route.

sectionName.description:
Listener the redirect route binds to. It must be the plaintext one: bound to every
listener, an HTTPS listener would redirect to itself forever.

Gateways to attach to, as `{name, namespace, sectionName}` entries. Empty attaches to the
Gateway this chart creates, when `gateway.create` is set.

Route timeouts, e.g. `{request: 300s}`. Worth raising: uploading a large scan through the

Certificates the listener terminates with, as `{name}` or `{name, namespace}` entries.

is the normal arrangement for both `ingress` and `gateway` below.

directly would let any client claim its plaintext request was encrypted.

Authentication delegated to a proxy in front of paperless — an OAuth2 proxy, an
authentication middleware, a service mesh — which authenticates the user and passes the
resulting name in a header.

clients usually authenticate with a token instead, and accepting both widens the surface.

the upstream fallback is a published constant, and a deployment running on it hands anybody
the ability to forge a session. Generate one with `openssl rand -base64 48`.

touch stored documents.

existingSecretKey.description: Key inside `existingSecret` that holds the broker password.
existingSecretKey.title: existingSecretKey

host.description: Broker host. Empty resolves to the bundled Valkey when `valkey.enabled` is set.
host.title: host

password.description:
Broker password. Ignored when `existingSecret` is set. It is injected into the URL at
container start rather than written into the ConfigMap, so it never appears in
`kubectl describe`. Passwords containing `@`, `/` or `:` must be percent-encoded, because
the value becomes part of a URL.
password.title: password

prefix.description:
Prefix for every key and channel, so several installs can share one broker without
consuming each other's tasks.
prefix.title: prefix

url.description:
Full broker URL (`redis://host:6379/0`, `rediss://…` for TLS), overriding every field
below. Use it for a managed service whose URL carries options this chart does not model.
A password embedded here ends up in the ConfigMap — put it in `redis.password` instead,
which keeps it in the Secret.
url.title: url

username.description: Broker username, for a server with ACLs configured.
username.title: username

redis.title: redis

replicaCount.description:
Number of replicas. paperless-ngx is a singleton: the pod also runs the scheduler and the
directory watcher, so a second replica double-schedules every periodic task and races the
first one for files in the consumption directory. Only `0` (stopped) and `1` are meaningful.
replicaCount.title: replicaCount

resourcesPreset.description:
Named resource sizing for the paperless-ngx container. Ignored when `resources` is set,
which it is by default — no preset is large enough for OCR.
resourcesPreset.title: resourcesPreset

revisionHistoryLimit.description: Number of old ReplicaSets retained for rollback.
revisionHistoryLimit.title: revisionHistoryLimit

securityContextPreset.description:
Container security context baseline. `restricted` drops all Linux capabilities and forbids
privilege escalation, running as root and a writable root filesystem.
securityContextPreset.title: securityContextPreset

annotations.description: Annotations for the Service, e.g. cloud load balancer configuration.
annotations.title: annotations

ipFamilyPolicy.description: IP family policy for the Service.
ipFamilyPolicy.title: ipFamilyPolicy

loadBalancerIP.description: Static IP to request for a LoadBalancer service.
loadBalancerIP.title: loadBalancerIP

loadBalancerSourceRanges.description: CIDRs allowed to reach the LoadBalancer. Empty means everywhere.
loadBalancerSourceRanges.title: loadBalancerSourceRanges

nodePort.description: Node port to pin under `NodePort` or `LoadBalancer`. `0` lets Kubernetes allocate one.
nodePort.title: nodePort

sessionAffinity.description: Session affinity. Irrelevant while `replicaCount` is 1, which it has to be.
sessionAffinity.title: sessionAffinity

type.description:
Service type. `ClusterIP` is right for the normal arrangement, where an Ingress or a
Gateway publishes the application and is the only thing that terminates TLS.
type.title: type

annotations.description: Additional annotations for the service account.
annotations.title: annotations

automountToken.description: Whether to automount the service account token.
automountToken.title: automountToken

create.description: Whether to create a dedicated service account.
create.title: create

name.description: Custom service account name (auto-generated if empty).
name.title: name

startupProbe.description:
Startup probe. Generous on purpose: the first start runs database migrations, builds the
search index and creates the superuser before the webserver accepts anything.

enabled.description: Enable the startup probe.
enabled.title: enabled

failureThreshold.description:
Consecutive failures before the container is considered failed. 60 x 10s covers a
ten-minute first start, which a large migration on slow storage genuinely takes.
failureThreshold.title: failureThreshold

httpGet.description:
HTTP handler for the probe. The path follows `paperless.rootPath`; an unauthenticated
request there is redirected to the login page, and a redirect counts as success.
httpGet.title: httpGet

startupProbe.title: startupProbe

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description:
Grace period for pod shutdown. Long enough for a task in flight to finish writing rather
than leaving a half-processed document behind.
terminationGracePeriodSeconds.title: terminationGracePeriodSeconds

tika.description:
Office and e-mail document support, provided by Apache Tika (text extraction) and Gotenberg
(rendering to PDF). Without it, `.docx`, `.odt`, `.xlsx` and `.eml` files are rejected at
consumption; PDFs and images never need it.

enabled.description:
Enable the Tika parser in paperless-ngx. Both endpoints below have to resolve, whether
they are bundled or external — the parser registers itself for those file types and then
fails every one of them if the services are not there.
enabled.title: enabled

gotenberg.description:
The Gotenberg server, which renders office documents and e-mail to PDF using LibreOffice
and Chromium.

allowList.description:
Regular expression limiting what Chromium may load. The default confines it to the
temporary directory the conversion request itself wrote, so tracking pixels, remote images
and in-cluster URLs are all unreachable.
allowList.title: allowList

disableJavaScript.description:
Disable JavaScript in the Chromium used to render `.eml` files. Leave it on: an e-mail
is untrusted input, and a headless browser executing whatever it contains is a
server-side request forgery primitive with a document library attached.
disableJavaScript.title: disableJavaScript

enabled.description:
Run Gotenberg as part of this release. Ignored when `tika.gotenberg.endpoint` names an
external one.
enabled.title: enabled

endpoint.description: URL of an external Gotenberg server (`http://gotenberg.example.svc:3000`).
endpoint.title: endpoint

pullPolicy.description: The image pull policy. Empty resolves automatically from the tag/digest.
pullPolicy.title: pullPolicy

registry.description: Registry host. Empty means Docker Hub.
registry.title: registry

repository.description:
Image repository. The default edition, which carries both LibreOffice and Chromium —
the trimmed `-chromium` and `-libreoffice` editions each break half of what paperless
asks Gotenberg to do.
repository.title: repository

resourcesPreset.description:
Named resource sizing. Ignored when `tika.gotenberg.resources` is set. LibreOffice and
Chromium are both memory-hungry; below `medium` conversions start failing rather than
slowing down.
resourcesPreset.title: resourcesPreset

gotenberg.title: gotenberg

server.description: The Apache Tika server, which extracts text and metadata from office documents.

enabled.description:
Run Tika as part of this release. Ignored when `tika.server.endpoint` names an external
one.
enabled.title: enabled

endpoint.description:
URL of an external Tika server (`http://tika.example.svc:9998`). Set this to use one
you already run, and the bundled server is not created.
endpoint.title: endpoint

pullPolicy.description: The image pull policy. Empty resolves automatically from the tag/digest.
pullPolicy.title: pullPolicy

registry.description: Registry host. Empty means Docker Hub.
registry.title: registry

repository.description:
Image repository. The plain image, not `-full`: paperless needs text extraction from
office formats, and the extra parsers in the full image cost roughly a gigabyte.
repository.title: repository

resourcesPreset.description:
Named resource sizing. Ignored when `tika.server.resources` is set. The JVM sizes its
heap from the memory limit, so shrinking this shrinks the largest document Tika can parse.
resourcesPreset.title: resourcesPreset

server.title: server

tika.title: tika

topologySpreadConstraints.description: Pod topology spread constraints for availability.
topologySpreadConstraints.title: topologySpreadConstraints

valkey.description:
A single-instance Valkey bundled with the release. Valkey is the Redis fork upstream's own
compose stack moved to. Evaluation tier, like the bundled PostgreSQL: one replica, no failover.

enabled.description:
Run Valkey as part of this release. On by default, because paperless-ngx cannot process a
single document without a broker and an install that silently does nothing is a worse
default than one extra pod.
enabled.title: enabled

pullPolicy.description: The image pull policy. Empty resolves automatically from the tag/digest.
pullPolicy.title: pullPolicy

registry.description: Registry host. Empty means Docker Hub.
registry.title: registry

enabled.description:
Persist the queue across restarts. Off by default: what lives here is a work queue, and
the cost of losing it is that documents already sitting in the consumption directory are
re-consumed on the next scan — while persisting it means a poison task survives every
restart. Turn it on when the consumption directory is a hand-fed drop box rather than a
watched share.
enabled.title: enabled

existingClaim.description: Use an existing PersistentVolumeClaim instead of the StatefulSet's own.
existingClaim.title: existingClaim

size.description: The storage size requested for the volume.
size.title: size

storageClassName.description: StorageClass for the claim. Empty uses the cluster default.
storageClassName.title: storageClassName

resourcesPreset.description: Named resource sizing for the broker container. Ignored when `valkey.resources` is set.
resourcesPreset.title: resourcesPreset

valkey.title: valkey
